posts.text:
Big 1st press conference for Fed Chair Kevin Warsh. The top takeaways:

1) He will tame inflation.  "[We] will deliver on price stability"
2) Market now pricing in 1 rate hike for 2026 and rising chance of 2.
3) The Warsh Fed will say less. Short statements. No forward guidance.
4) He's launching 5 tasks forces that are similar to what consulting firms do...look at what Fed doing and make recommendations for change.
Stay tuned: Big change is coming in 2027

posts.text:
Kevin Warsh's 1st press conference begins with 3 big messages:

1) Inflation: "This committee will deliver price stability"
2) No forward guidance. "We agreed [it] was not well suited for the current policy juncture." Dot Plot will continue, but Warsh won't participate
3) Warsh launching 5 task forces to "propose next steps" for policymaker consideration, including on Fed communication

posts.text:
Wow. I just got my latest electric bill.

Exact same daily usage as last year
Exact same daily avg. temp as last year
But... a nearly 30% increase in the daily avg. cost

(The official CPI report says electricity costs are up 6% in the past year. Obviously, it varies by region)

posts.text:
Inflation is so high that it's erasing all wage gains.

Inflation: 4.2% in May for the past year
Wage growth: 3.4% in May for the past year.

Americans are getting squeezed financially. This isn't just "bad vibes" about the economy. There is real pain, especially for middle-class and lower-income households. It's tough because so many basic items are seeing sizable price increases: gas, electricity, food, medical care.

posts.text:
Great chart from Nick showing the labor market rebound. The hiring recession is over. More firms are hiring again. It’s getting easier to find a job (though not a job that will offer raises above inflation)


Nick Timiraos (@NickTimiraos)

The U.S. economy added 172,000 jobs in May and the unemployment rate held at 4.3%.

There were large upward revisions to March and April, raising the three- and six-month hiring averages to 188,000 and 92,000, respectively.





— https://nitter.net/NickTimira

posts.text:
Another encouraging sign: The Black Unemployment rate fell to 6.6% in May.

That's the lowest in a year.

The Black unemployment rate is often seen as a leading indicator. The fact that it's improving is another good sign (and an indicator that more Americans are benefitting from job gains this year)
